subject.title: macOS update can leave manual-update loop and stale node host causing Gateway restart storm

question: Should the macOS same-version/manual update path short-circuit before service stop/restart, or should OpenClaw keep the refresh path and harden stale-job cleanup plus launchd/node recovery around it?
rationale: Current source supports multiple plausible repairs, but choosing between no-op short-circuit, durable refresh semantics, and broader stale-job cleanup changes the user-visible update contract.

options.title: Short-circuit no-op updates
options.body: Treat package already-current updates as a successful no-op before managed service stop/restart, then add a separate stale-job doctor cleanup for known legacy labels.

options.title: Harden refresh semantics
options.body: Keep same-version package refresh behavior but add dedupe, full launchd health verification, broader stale updater cleanup, and node-host restart proof before closing.

options.title: Split remaining work
options.body: Move UI/update.run no-op policy, stale `manualupdate` cleanup, and node skew into separate canonical issues, then close this only after those links preserve the field evidence.

recommendation.title: Short-circuit no-op updates
recommendation.body: Treat package already-current updates as a successful no-op before managed service stop/restart, then add a separate stale-job doctor cleanup for known legacy labels.
